actions.name: Disseminate TrickBot and BazarLoader via phishing campaigns
actions.description: Cybercriminals disseminate TrickBot and BazarLoader via phishing campaigns that contain either links to malicious websites that host the malware or attachments with the malware.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: TrickBot copies itself as an executable with a random 12-character filename and places it in system directories
actions.description: After successful execution of the malware, TrickBot copies itself as an executable file with a 12-character (includes .exe), randomly generated file name and places this file in one of the following directories: C:\Windows\, C:\Windows\SysWOW64\, or C:\Users\[Username]\AppData\Roaming\.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: TrickBot establishes communication with C2 servers and downloads modules
actions.description: Once the executable is running and successful in establishing communication with C2s, the executable places appropriate modules downloaded from C2s for the infected processor architecture type (32 or 64 bit instruction set), to the infected host’s %APPDATA% or %PROGRAMDATA% directory.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: TrickBot uses scheduled tasks every 15 minutes for persistence
actions.description: The malware uses scheduled tasks that run every 15 minutes to ensure persistence on the victim machine. The scheduled task typically uses the naming convention autoupdate#[5_random_numbers].
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: TrickBot deploys malicious batch scripts using PowerShell commands
actions.description: After successful execution, anchor_dns further deploys malicious batch scripts (.bat) using PowerShell commands.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: TrickBot executes self-deletion commands
actions.description: The malware deploys self-deletion techniques by executing commands such as cmd.exe /c timeout 3 && del C:\Users\[username]\[malware_sample] and cmd.exe /C PowerShell "Start-Sleep 3; Remove-Item C:\Users\[username]\[malware_sample_location]\".
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: BazarLoader infection via phishing emails with links to malware payloads
actions.description: BazarLoader malware is typically deployed via phishing emails containing links to actor-controlled Google Drive documents or other free online filehosting solutions, which contain links to URLs hosting malware payloads in the form of misnamed or multiple extension files.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Ryuk ransomware deployed as payload from banking Trojans such as TrickBot
actions.description: Typically Ryuk has been deployed as a payload from banking Trojans such as TrickBot.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Ryuk actors use commercial off-the-shelf tools to steal credentials
actions.description: While negotiating the victim network, Ryuk actors commonly use commercial off-the-shelf products such as Cobalt Strike and PowerShell Empire to steal credentials, allowing them to dump clear text passwords or hash values from memory with the use of Mimikatz.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Ryuk actors maintain persistence using scheduled tasks and service creation
actions.description: In order to maintain persistence in the victim environment, Ryuk actors have been known to use scheduled tasks and service creation.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Ryuk actors map network and enumerate environment using native tools
actions.description: Ryuk actors quickly map the network to enumerate the environment using native tools such as net view, net computers, and ping to locate mapped network shares, domain controllers, and active directory.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Ryuk actors move laterally using native and third-party tools
actions.description: To move laterally throughout the network, Ryuk actors rely on native tools such as PowerShell, Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI), Windows Remote Management, and Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), as well as third-party tools like Bloodhound.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Ryuk encrypts files using AES-256 and RSA public key
actions.description: Once dropped, Ryuk uses AES-256 to encrypt files and an RSA public key to encrypt the AES key.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Ryuk dropper deletes backup files and Volume Shadow Copies
actions.description: The Ryuk dropper drops a .bat file that attempts to delete all backup files and Volume Shadow Copies, preventing the victim from recovering encrypted files without the decryption program.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Ryuk actors attempt to shut down or uninstall security applications
actions.description: Attackers attempt to shut down or uninstall security applications on victim systems that might prevent the ransomware from executing, normally via a script but capable of manual removal if needed.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.
